subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool capacity increase + tokens/sec SLO addendum
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool capacity increase + tokens/sec SLO addendum

Hi Elaine,

As we approach your renewal (term runs out 2026-03-15) I wanted to capture the capacity and SLO changes we discussed on last week's call. FintechCo's usage pattern indicates a steady uptick in high-throughput inference during peak batch windows — you asked for both additional reserved GPUs and clear throughput guarantees.

Attached is a first-pass addendum draft and a capacity estimate sheet. High-level proposal:
- Increase Reserved Pool from 12 A100-equivalent GPUs to 20 (8 additional).
- Add tokens/sec SLO: guaranteed sustained baseline of 9,000 tokens/sec for the reserved pool measured as a 5-minute rolling window; 99.9% monthly availability target.
- Burst allowance: up to 50% above baseline for 10-minute windows, subject to available spare capacity.
- Credits: service credit equivalent to 5% of monthly committed fee for each 30-min SLO breach window after the first occurrence; escalates to 15% for repeated breaches (3+ distinct days in a month).
- Measurement & reporting: Redwood to expose per-pool tokens/sec metrics via Console + audit CSV; metric source: runtime token emission count aggregated per pool.

Questions for you: is the tokens/sec metric acceptable vs RPS/latency? Do you want a lower baseline + larger burst, or the baseline above? Also, are you okay extending the renewal term to 12 months from the current 6 for the committed capacity step-up?

If that looks reasonable I can push an updated addendum for procurement review (tracked via DocuSign link in HubSpot).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to finalize wording.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0136

Attachments: 20260225-dedicated-addendum-draft.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), capacity-estimate-sheet.xlsx (Excel, 2 tabs)

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool capacity increase + tokens/sec SLO addendum

Marcus,

Thanks for the write-up and the draft. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Metric definition: we need the SLO tied to user-facing throughput (tokens/sec as seen by calls to the public API) but also want an optional RPS/latency floor so we don't trade throughput for extreme latency. Can you include both tokens/sec (primary) and p95 latency target per request (secondary)?

2) Measurement windows: 5-minute rolling baseline is fine; for credits we prefer daily windows (anyday with >1 hour of breach contributes to credit calculus). Can you map your 30-min windows to our daily-based approach?

3) Credits: procurement will push back on per-incident credit escalation. Is Redwood open to a single capped credit schedule instead (e.g., up to 10% monthly credit for repeated breaches) rather than progressive escalation?

4) Pricing: need the delta for 8 GPUs expressed as committed monthly fee + per-token overage rate for burst.

We can do a short review with procurement next Tuesday. Can you have an updated addendum + concrete pricing numbers by EOD Monday?

Appreciate it — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
elaine.park@fintechco.com

Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Dedicated pool capacity increase + tokens/sec SLO addendum

Internal — quick alignment:

Elaine pushed back on escalation-style credits and wants p95 latency included as a secondary metric. Procurement asks for daily breach accounting. They also want committed monthly delta + token overage price. Laura, can you run numbers for committed fee (+8 GPUs) and a per-token overage band for burst? Naomi, can you propose SLO wording that maps our runtime tokens/sec metric to a public API tokens/sec measurement and include tolerances for maintenance? Monica, we may want a 12-month term to smooth pricing; procurement might prefer 6 months, expect negotiation.

Turnaround: EOD Monday for updated addendum so we can be on their Tuesday slot. If we need legal, I can loop Markus (legal) but try to keep it engineering + commercial first.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Updated addendum + pricing for capacity increase (attached)

Elaine / Tom,

Per our internal alignment, attached is an updated addendum draft that:
- Defines primary SLO as tokens/sec measured at the ingress API (Redwood proxy) with a mapping clause that reconciles any internal pool accounting differences.
- Adds p95 request latency target of < 220 ms for production inference calls as a secondary, non-credit-bearing metric; sustained p95 violations will trigger joint investigation and prioritization lanes but not automatic credits.
- Measurement: baseline sustained tokens/sec defined as 5-minute rolling median; credit calculation will convert our 30-min breach windows into daily breach tallies for procurement compatibility (we'll count days with > 60 cumulative minutes of breach toward credit eligibility).
- Credits: single capped schedule up to 10% monthly credit (agreed cap) for repeated breaches; first incident in a month waived to allow for transient infra events.
- Pricing: committed monthly fee delta for +8 GPUs: $95,000/month; token overage for burst usage above committed baseline: $0.0009 per token (tiered bands apply, see sheet).
- Term: proposed 12-month renewal with a 30-day ramp where we provision 4 GPUs immediately and the remaining 4 within 45 days.

I've attached: 20260225-dedicated-addendum-draft.pdf (updated) and capacity-estimate-sheet.xlsx with the pricing bands and ramp schedule.

If that aligns, please say so and we'll send the final DocuSign packet to procurement. If you want different credit language or a different measurement mapping, call out the exact clause and we'll iterate.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity. Procurement reviewed the pricing bands and the single capped credit schedule and they are okay to proceed with the 12-month term with the 30/45-day ramp. Two final asks before DocuSign:

1) Please add an explicit scheduled maintenance blackout window: no emergency maintenance on overlaps with our daily 09:00-11:00 PST batch run unless mutually agreed.
2) Confirm that the tokens/sec telemetry will be delivered via a daily CSV export (s3 link) in addition to the Console dashboard.

If you can append those two bullets to the addendum and resend I can authorize procurement to sign.

Signed off — Tom (pending the two small edits).
